main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling food (sambal belacan) in the shared kitchen; settled on D cooking it only on weekends.

A-B.evidence: A asks for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B agrees (T2). A later accepts cooking after 7 (T11), while B wants weekends only (T17), and A never comments on the weekend deal.

A-C.evidence: C complains about laundry smell (T3) in support of A's concern. A accepts cooking after 7 (T11), C accepts weekends (T20). The two never address each other.

A-D.evidence: D refuses to stop cooking (T4). A shares work hours (T5, T7), D offers to cook later (T6), and A accepts: 'If you cook after 7, that works for me' (T11).

B-C.evidence: Both object to the smell (T2, T3, T8, T9), both reject D's door and laundry fix (T13, T14), and both accept weekends only (T19, T20).

B-D.evidence: B rejects cooking after 7 (T8) and the door-closing fix (T13); B proposes weekends (T17) and D agrees: 'Weekends I can do' (T18).

C-D.evidence: C rejects the laundry fix (T14). D accepts weekends (T18) and C replies 'Weekends are fine for me too. Thanks, Agent D' (T20).
